78895.subject: 🔷 The Daily: Nasdaq is investing $100M in Kraken's parent at a $21B valuation
78895.body:
Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong says bitcoin has bottomed for current cycle, expects uptrend over next two years | Researchers halve quantum resource benchmark for key operation in Bitcoin, Ethereum attack | MoneyGram launches first stablecoin-backed Visa card in Colombia | Trezor says third-party security breach led to phishing emails from legitimate domain |

The Daily ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by James Hunt | Edited by Jason Shubnell

Presented By:

( https://bron.org/?utm_source=TheBlock&utm_medium=Email&utm_campaign=DailyNewsletter&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Happy Thursday! *Bitcoin* is testing support around $77,000 after a hotter-than-expected *PPI* print, with *21Shares' Matt Mena* eyeing tomorrow's *CPI* data as the next catalyst for a move in either direction.

In today's newsletter, *Nasdaq* plans a $100 million investment in *Kraken's* parent company, *Brian Armstrong* says *bitcoin* has bottomed, researchers halve a *quantum* resource benchmark for attacking *Bitcoin* , and more.

Meanwhile, *Citadel Securities* urges ( https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-09-10-citadel-urges-sec-assert-oversight-event-contracts-tied-public-firms-414140?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) the *SEC* to assert oversight of event contracts tied to public firms.

*P.S.* Don't forget to check out The Funding , a biweekly rundown of crypto VC trends. It's a great read — and just like The Daily, it's free to subscribe ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters?select=The+Funding&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) !

*THE BIG ONE*

*💰 Nasdaq to invest $100 million in Kraken parent Payward as firms expand partnership*

( https://www.theblock.co/news/deals/2026-09-10-nasdaq-to-invest-100-million-in-kraken-parent-payward-as-firms-expand-partnership-414120?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*Nasdaq's* venture arm agreed to invest $100 million in *Payward* , crypto exchange *Kraken's* parent company, deepening their partnership on tokenized equities and market infrastructure.

* The deal values Payward at $21 billion, per Bloomberg, and will see the firm adopt Nasdaq's market surveillance technology across its crypto, equities, tokenized equities, futures, and options venues.
* The firms are also targeting a second-quarter 2027 launch of *Nasdaq Equity Tokens* , or NETs, connecting them to Payward's *xStocks* ecosystem.
* Payward co-CEO *Arjun Sethi* said onchain settlement removes the wait from the U.S. clearing system, while keeping shareholder rights intact.
* Nasdaq President *Tal Cohen* said the investment reflects confidence that Payward can help build infrastructure to move capital while preserving trust and transparency.

Discover the factors threatening the dominance of the world's reserve currency. Want more content from In Context? Sign up here to receive weekly insights directly in your inbox. The US–Canada trade war is escalating. What’s next? Trade negotiations between the U.S. and Canada broke down on August 21. In response, the Trump administration instituted 50% tariffs on a broad range of Canadian exports, including dairy products and alcoholic beverages, which came into effect on August 22. The administration has also threatened to increase tariffs on Canadian autos and auto parts to 50% — doubling the current rate of 25% — from January 1, 2027. Consequently, Canada imposed dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs beginning September 8, with individual product rates based on the matching U.S. rate for the same goods. “This increase in effective tariff rates on Canada is large enough to suggest some additional downside risk for a Canadian economy that had appeared poised for a mid-year rebound after contracting around the start of the year,” said Michael Hanson, a senior economist at J.P.
